rules.statement: Accept an authority or endpoint URL only if it uses `https`, or `http` on a loopback host (`Uri.IsLoopback`). Check the raw string as well as the parsed `Uri`: it must start with its scheme, contain no whitespace and have no fragment, and an authority must also have no query.
rules.why: Plain http may only reach the same machine, which still lets tests run against an in-process OP. Checking the raw string closes the gaps that lenient `Uri` parsing leaves open.
rules.check: Look for code that accepts an authority, discovery endpoint or jwks_uri without the https-or-loopback-http check, or that validates only `Uri.Scheme` and skips the whitespace, fragment and query checks on the raw string.

rules.statement: When fetching OpenID Provider discovery metadata, require the returned `issuer` to equal the configured authority string by ordinal comparison. Require `token_endpoint` and `jwks_uri`, and apply the endpoint URL rule to every endpoint member that is present.
rules.why: OIDC Discovery §4.3 requires an exact issuer match. Endpoints taken from metadata must meet the same transport rules as configured ones.
rules.check: Look for an issuer comparison that ignores case, trims, normalizes or is missing, and for endpoint members of discovery metadata used without validation.

rules.statement: A cache of remote protocol metadata or keys may serve its last good value after a failed refresh, within a bounded stale lifetime. It must never relax validation to do so. It must collapse concurrent misses into one fetch, rate-limit forced refreshes, and throw when the first fetch fails.
rules.why: This keeps the client available when the OP fails briefly, without weakening security and without hammering the OP.
rules.check: Look for cache code that skips validation for stale or fallback values, lets concurrent misses each start a fetch, puts no limit on forced refreshes (for example on an unknown `kid`), or invents a value when the first fetch fails.

rules.statement: When importing a remote JWKS for signature verification: skip each key that cannot be used (not an object, not a parseable JWK, `use` other than `sig`, `key_ops` without `verify`, a non-asymmetric or unknown key type, or material that fails to import). Refuse the whole set if it carries private or symmetric material, has two usable keys with the same `kid`, or has no usable key.
rules.why: RFC 7517 §5 says unusable keys are ignored. A set that exposes secrets or has an ambiguous `kid` cannot be trusted at all.
rules.check: Look for JWKS import that accepts private or `oct` keys, ignores `use` or `key_ops`, silently keeps the first or last key of a duplicate `kid`, or returns an empty key set instead of failing.

rules.statement: Read a protocol client's credentials (client secrets, signing keys) from a named, keyed secret-key provider (key ring), never from configuration values.
rules.why: Credentials in configuration cannot rotate and put secrets in configuration. A key ring supports rotation and keys held in a KMS.
rules.check: Look for client secrets or private keys bound from `IConfiguration` or options properties instead of resolved from a keyed key-ring provider.

rules.statement: Use the family's own JOSE/JWT stack (`NCode.Identity.Jose`/`Jwt` abstractions) for OpenID/OAuth client work, not `Microsoft.IdentityModel` or the ASP.NET Core OpenID Connect handler.
rules.why: Those libraries bring a second JOSE stack, with a second key and algorithm policy.
rules.check: Look for new references to `Microsoft.IdentityModel.*` or `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect` in protocol client code.

rules.statement: In a `private_key_jwt` client assertion, set `aud` to the OP's issuer as a single string, not the token endpoint URL and not an array. Set `iss` and `sub` to the client id, `jti` to 16 random bytes in base64url, `iat`/`nbf` to now, and `exp` to a fixed short lifetime (60 seconds).
rules.why: RFC 7523bis and FAPI 2.0 require the issuer as the audience.
rules.check: Look for assertions whose `aud` is the token endpoint or an array, whose `jti` is not random, or whose lifetime is long or configurable.

rules.statement: Sign client assertions only with asymmetric keys. Never pick `none`, and validate configured algorithm lists (no blank entry, no `none`, no duplicate).
rules.why: A MAC or `none` must never be used to sign an assertion.
rules.check: Look for algorithm selection that can choose a symmetric key, an HS* algorithm or `none`, or a configured algorithm list that is not validated.

rules.statement: In `client_secret_basic`, form-urlencode the client id and the secret before joining them with ':' and base64-encoding the result.
rules.check: Look for Basic authorization headers built from raw client_id:secret without form-urlencoding.

rules.statement: Return an OAuth error response (a JSON object with a string `error`, at any status) to the caller as a value. Throw a provider exception, with the cause as the inner exception, for transport failures, timeouts, oversized bodies, invalid JSON, non-error non-2xx responses or incomplete success responses. Let caller cancellation propagate as `OperationCanceledException`.
rules.why: Callers need errors such as `invalid_grant` as values, not as exceptions. Other failures must keep their cause.
rules.check: Look for code that throws on OAuth error responses, wraps caller cancellation, drops the inner exception, or treats a non-JSON failure as an OAuth error.

rules.statement: Throw `InvalidOperationException` for configuration errors found at call time, such as a missing key ring, an unknown authentication method, or an operation the provider's metadata does not support.
rules.why: These are misconfigurations, not protocol failures, so they must stay distinct from provider exceptions.
rules.check: Look for configuration errors reported as protocol/provider exceptions or returned as error values.

rules.statement: Make outbound HTTP to an identity provider through a named client whose primary handler disables automatic redirects and cookies. Bound each request with a timeout and each response with a maximum body size.
rules.why: Then a hostile or misconfigured provider cannot redirect the client or exhaust its memory.
rules.check: Look for `HttpClient` usage against an OP with `AllowAutoRedirect` left on, cookies enabled, no timeout, or a response body read without a size cap.

rules.statement: Never parse an empty HTTP response body as JSON, whatever its media type. Parse JSON only for the expected JSON media types.
rules.why: Some valid responses, such as a successful RFC 7009 revocation, have an empty body.
rules.check: Look for JSON deserialization of response content without a check for an empty body or for the media type.

rules.statement: Register pluggable strategy implementations (such as client authentication methods) with `TryAddEnumerable`, select them by name, and throw when two registrations share a name.
rules.why: Vocabularies are open: a new method is a registration with no library change, and a duplicate name must fail fast instead of being ambiguous.
rules.check: Look for a closed switch over strategy names, registration with `AddSingleton` that allows duplicates, or name collisions resolved silently.

rules.statement: An authorization-code token request must include a PKCE `code_verifier`.
rules.why: The decision requires PKCE on every authorization-code request the client sends.
rules.check: Look for authorization-code request types or calls where `code_verifier` is optional or missing.

rules.statement: Do not add metrics for outbound HTTP calls that `System.Net.Http` already measures.
rules.check: Look for new counters or histograms around HttpClient calls that duplicate the built-in HTTP client metrics.

rules.statement: An implementation package references only abstraction packages of other components, not their implementation packages.
rules.why: Implementation packages depend only on abstractions.
rules.check: Look for a ProjectReference or PackageReference from an implementation project to another component's non-Abstractions package.
